user_profile_example._note: A real potential customer. PGDM Finance graduate joining startup and SME advisory work. Declared knowledge and gaps taken verbatim from what they told us.
user_profile_example.background: PGDM, Finance specialisation. Excel-based financial models and valuation projects during the course. Heading into startup fundraising and SME IPO advisory.
user_profile_example._gap_commentary: They asked for 'valuation revision' and 'advanced Excel'. What they actually lack is the startup-specific layer: unit economics, cap table mechanics, ESOP dilution, and the ability to audit a model rather than build one. A finance graduate advising startups will spend more time finding errors in a founder's model than building their own — and that skill is not taught in a PGDM.

what_jintu_offers_today.excel-at-work: Covers most of their Excel gaps directly — 20 days.
what_jintu_offers_today.thinking-under-uncertainty: Relevant to diligence judgement and base rates — 24 days.
what_jintu_offers_today.writing-clearly: Not built yet. Directly relevant: investment memos and pitch narrative.

user_profile_example.the_honest_answer: Jintu has no finance roadmap. Excel at work covers roughly a third of what they need. The startup finance and SME IPO material — which is the majority of their stated gap and the whole of their job — does not exist yet.
